what: One motor turns a carrier around a stationary 16-tooth sun gear. An 8-tooth idler and an 8-tooth planet ride on the carrier. Their two external meshes make the planet turn once backward for each forward carrier turn. A bar on the planet has two markers equally far from its shaft. Each marker follows a straight line, and their lines are perpendicular. The planet center follows a circle. There are no sliding guides at the markers. One motor turns a carrier whose two moving 8T gears orbit a fixed 16T sun. The planet counterrotates, so two equal-radius markers trace perpendicular 80 mm straight strokes while their shaft follows a circle of radius 20 mm. Compare two speeds and reversal, then remove only the stationary sun gear.
try: Open the matching model and finite program, reset to the saved pose and use the plain mat. Motor A drives the 60-tooth carrier ring through a 20-tooth pinion. Distinguish motor turns from carrier turns: their increments have a magnitude ratio of three to one and opposite directions. Read the validation record for the tested scope.

Watch one complete carrier revolution. Count the idler and planet turns relative to the chassis, then count the planet turns relative to the rotating carrier. Track both actual tile centers as well as the center of the planet shaft. Predict why the center follows a circle while the two tiles follow straight strokes.

Compare a full forward turn and return at carrier speed magnitudes of 20 and 30 degrees per second. The finite program records five seconds of free startup, explicitly homes the input from its current encoder reading, then visits quarter-turn targets with settling and observation intervals. The output arm has no motor.

Reset and run the comparison with only the stationary sun gear removed. Leave the moving idler, planet, all shafts, bearings and retainers in place. Repeat the same motor program. Compare the observed planet phase and both full marker positions with their coupled predictions at matched carrier angles. Do not assume that the released gear pair remains still or that it must draw a particular replacement curve.
why: Let theta be the carrier angle, alpha the idler angle and phi the planet angle, all measured in the chassis plane. In the rotating carrier frame, the two external gear meshes give 16(0-theta)+8(alpha-theta)=constant and 8(alpha-theta)+8(phi-theta)=constant. Their increments imply delta alpha=3 delta theta and delta phi=-delta theta. For carrier radius r and equal marker radius r, Pplus=r(cos theta,sin theta)+r(cos phi,sin phi) and Pminus=r(cos theta,sin theta)-r(cos phi,sin phi). If the authored gear clock gives phi=-theta+delta, these points lie on perpendicular fixed lines at delta/2 and delta/2+90 degrees. The fixed line directions come from the saved geometry, not a fit to the measured path.
matters: A straight output path can result from the sum of two circular motions. The gearing enforces the required counterrotation, while equal radii make one transverse component cancel. Both geometry and phase matter. Removing the fixed reaction gear releases the angular reference even though the two moving gears remain meshed.
question: The carrier radius and each marker radius are 20 mm. What are the full marker strokes, the planet-center orbit radius, and the idler and planet rotation increments for one carrier turn? What changes if a marker is placed at radius q instead of r?
answer: Each marker has an 80 mm full stroke, and the planet center follows a circle of radius 20 mm. Relative to the chassis, the idler turns three times in the carrier direction and the planet turns once in the opposite direction. Relative to the carrier, the planet turns twice backward. A marker at unequal radius q follows an ellipse with semiaxes r+q and abs(r-q), rotated by half the fixed gear-clock phase. Changing the marker requires a new physical model and clearance qualification.
further: Observe actual tip_plus and tip_minus tile centers and the planet shaft from their own rigid bodies. Evaluate the two full-vector predictions from independently measured carrier motion. Show predicted paths separately from measured paths. A nearly stationary marker on the nominal line is not evidence of a useful straight-line machine: measure the full stroke as well.

At an extreme of one marker stroke, the other marker passes through the line crossing. Their signed positions are cosine and sine components of the same carrier phase. Compare equal carrier-angle intervals near the center and near a stroke endpoint; uniform rotation does not produce uniform linear speed.

Compare Straight Eight, Ellipse Engine, Offset Orbit and Orbit Mixer. They use a linkage, sliding trammel, offset shaft coupling and planetary heading control. Circle Splitter uses a fixed sun and two moving external gears to combine equal opposite rotations. The complete package records the ordinary inferred gear and bearing behavior; its native residuals are not physical hardware precision or torque ratings.
formula: For theta=carrier phase, phi=-theta+delta and r=20 mm: A=r(cos theta,sin theta); Pplus=A+r(cos phi,sin phi)=2r cos(theta-delta/2)(cos(delta/2),sin(delta/2)); Pminus=A-r(cos phi,sin phi)=2r sin(theta-delta/2)(-sin(delta/2),cos(delta/2)). Each full stroke is 4r=80 mm. Delta alpha=3 delta theta; delta phi=-delta theta; delta(phi-theta)=-2 delta theta. The authored geometry supplies the phase constant and line axes before execution.
